subject.title: [Feature]: Global (IP-agnostic) auth rate limiting option for public-exposed deployments

question: Should Gateway auth support a permanent default-off IP-agnostic failed-auth lockout mode for public password/token deployments?
rationale: The code change is mechanically small, but it changes the Gateway auth brute-force boundary and introduces an intentional all-client lockout failure mode under attack.

options.title: Accept after security fixes
options.body: Sponsor the opt-in core config only after the linked PR fixes loopback reset behavior, documents the all-client lockout tradeoff, and posts real Gateway proof.

options.title: Keep policy external
options.body: Keep core per-IP only and document identity-aware proxy, long random credentials, or external operational controls for public deployments.

options.title: Defer broader hardening
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers settle the wider public-exposure hardening direction, including password strength and global lockout policy.

recommendation.title: Accept after security fixes
recommendation.body: Sponsor the opt-in core config only after the linked PR fixes loopback reset behavior, documents the all-client lockout tradeoff, and posts real Gateway proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest routing signal for Gateway auth security policy from merged rate-limit history and adjacent auth hardening work.
